object_types.name: Person
object_types.definition: A person in the system with a unique person ID.

source_references.excerpt: We track persons generally -- anyone in the system is a person with a person ID.

object_types.name: Employee
object_types.definition: A person who works in the organization and is assigned to a department.

source_references.excerpt: Employees are persons; every employee is also a person, identified the same way.

object_types.name: Manager
object_types.definition: An employee with extra responsibilities for managing a department.

source_references.excerpt: A manager is an employee with extra responsibilities. Every manager is an employee, and through that, a person.

object_types.name: Department
object_types.definition: An organizational unit with a unique department code and name.

source_references.excerpt: Each department has a department code. Departments also each have a department name, like "Payroll" or "Field Operations", and no two share a name.

object_types.name: PersonId
object_types.definition: The unique identifier for a person.

source_references.excerpt: We track persons generally -- anyone in the system is a person with a person ID.

object_types.name: DepartmentCode
object_types.definition: The unique code identifying a department.

source_references.excerpt: Each department has a department code.

object_types.name: DepartmentName
object_types.definition: The name of a department, unique across all departments.

source_references.excerpt: Departments also each have a department name, like "Payroll" or "Field Operations", and no two share a name.
We track persons generally -- anyone in the system is a person with a person ID.
Each department has a department code.
Departments also each have a department name, like "Payroll" or "Field Operations", and no two share a name.
Every employee works in exactly one department. Departments have many employees, but nobody is in two departments at once, and nobody is unassigned.
A manager manages at most one department. Some managers are between assignments and manage none.

ambiguities.description: Department identification: The transcript states that each department has a department code and that no two departments share a name. It is unclear whether department_code or department_name (or both) serve as the primary reference scheme for identification. Currently, reference_mode is set to 'department_code', but department_name could also be a unique identifier. Are both attributes candidate identifiers, or is only one the preferred reference mode?

ambiguities.description: Manager-Department relationship optionality: The transcript states 'A manager manages at most one department' and 'Some managers are between assignments and manage none.' This clearly indicates that not every manager manages a department (i.e., the relationship is optional on the manager side). However, it does not explicitly state whether every department must be managed by a manager or whether a department can exist without a manager. Is the Manager manages Department relationship mandatory on the Department side?

source_references.excerpt: A manager manages at most one department. Some managers are between assignments and manage none.

ambiguities.description: Employee-Department relationship direction clarity: The transcript states 'Every employee works in exactly one department' and 'Departments have many employees.' This establishes a one-to-many (many employees per department) relationship, but it does not explicitly address whether an employee can work in multiple departments over time or only one at a single point in time. Additionally, it is unclear whether historical tracking of department changes is required or if only current assignment is modeled.

source_references.excerpt: Every employee works in exactly one department. Departments have many employees, but nobody is in two departments at once, and nobody is unassigned.
